planned_entries.w_pd_1_limb: (b) cross-day pattern no single operational entry surfaces + (c) strategic shift in how vulnerability triage must be run
planned_entries.thesis: Four flaws this week had their exploitation status contradicted between authorities, in BOTH directions — CISA KEV vs vendor 'not exploited' twice, a vendor correcting itself while ENISA's exploited feed kept the old value, and one flaw patched before any CVE existed. A triage queue ordered on any single authority's exploitation field mis-ranked all four.
components: CVE-2026-33824 (Windows IKEEXT) — CISA KEV 2026-08-18, EPSS 55.85; MSRC record unrevised since 14 April, still 'Exploitation Less Likely', exploitation=no
CVE-2026-55040 (SharePoint) — CISA KEV 2026-08-18; MSRC record unrevised since 14 July, exploitation=no
CVE-2026-69836 (Entra ID, CVSS 10.0) — MSRC revision 1.1 of 2026-08-21 corrected to not-exploited; ENISA EUVD re-synced 2026-08-22 still carries it on the exploited feed
CVE-2026-73570 (Zimbra zimbra-snmp) — fix shipped 2026-07-21 with no CVE at all; identifier published 2026-08-13; recorded exploited 2026-08-18
planned_entries.cves_field: [] — per-CVE metadata belongs to the operational entries that own it; the gate FAILs CVE-level duplication upward

planned_entries.thesis: Six unrelated items this week turned on vendor-supplied functionality behaving exactly as designed — there was no vulnerability to patch and no artefact to blocklist. The control surface is configuration and telemetry, not a fix.
components: Akira: Safe Mode with Networking + the Safe Mode service allow-list, a documented Windows boot mode (2026-08-17)

BTR.sys: a functionally required, Microsoft-signed Defender component extracted from MpEngine.dll; MSRC declined to service it and it cannot be blocklisted without breaking Defender remediation (2026-08-23)
GTIG's three Russia-nexus clusters: application-specific passwords, device-code approval, WhatsApp device-linking — all legitimate authentication workflows the victim completes (2026-08-23)
Ray: the dashboard's unauthenticated job-submission endpoints are by design; authentication first exists in 2.52.0 and is off by default (2026-08-18)
Metabase: the credential store is the product's purpose, and Metabase's own guidance is that patching does not invalidate credentials already exposed (2026-08-19)
TrueConf: the server's own client-installer distribution channel is what delivers the trojanised build to meeting attendees (2026-08-23)
planned_entries.dedup_guard: MUST NOT re-list 2026-08-16/weekly-w33-kernel-rootkits-edit-what-windows-reports (kernel rootkits altering what the OS reports) or 2026-08-16/weekly-w33-attacking-the-record-not-the-sensor (anti-forensics against the post-incident record). This lens is neither: it is the absence of any patchable or blocklistable artefact. Reference both W33 entries explicitly to mark the boundary.

planned_entries.w_pd_1_limb: (b) cross-day pattern — four unrelated disclosures, four different lifecycle stages
planned_entries.thesis: Four unrelated in-window disclosures put AI inside the attacker's own workflow rather than in a vendor's marketing, at four different stages: exploitation research, tool development, social engineering, and malware engineering.
components: Talos recovered UAT-10147's own AI-generated nine-section ViewState playbook and four companion Python scripts from an open directory (2026-08-20)
The five-agency S7 advisory describes AI-developed Python tooling built on snap7.dll / python-snap7, dressed as legitimate OT monitoring software (2026-08-19)
Insikt's PurpleDelta analysis records AI-generated photos and purpose-configured chatbot assistants answering interview questions in real time (2026-08-18)

Bitdefender assesses SilkParasite as AI-*assisted* rather than AI-generated, and names the tells — leftover Go test functions, placeholder encryption keys, shared cross-language architecture, without the degradation generated code shows (2026-08-19)
planned_entries.note: SilkParasite is new this run (W1) and is published as its own weekly-research entry; this synthesis cites it inline, not via references.

planned_entries.w_pd_1_limb: (b) cross-day pattern across five European public-sector disclosures
planned_entries.thesis: In every European public-administration compromise disclosed this week, the party that established what happened was not the monitoring meant to catch it — and in two of them nobody established it at all.
components: Latvia CSDD — own staff found and stopped it within hours; the provider contracted for round-the-clock monitoring neither detected nor alerted (2026-08-20)
Martigny-Combe (VS) — eight days of undetected mailbox access, surfaced only when the attacker mass-mailed ~450 of the commune's own contacts (2026-08-23)
HWZ Zurich — learned the shape of its own breach from the extortion group's leak-site listing naming eight customer domains; HWZ itself names no provider (2026-08-23)
Arbeiterkammer Oberösterreich — cannot scope at all because the attackers wiped the traces, so every member is notified under Article 34 as a precaution (2026-08-18)
Berlin Landesnetz — a week on, no named authority has stated a vector, a product or a CVE, so no peer administration can learn a defensive lesson from it (W2 finding, 2026-08-17..23)
planned_entries.dedup_guard: MUST NOT re-list 2026-08-16/weekly-w33-compromised-party-was-not-the-notifying-party, whose lens was the displacement of the NOTIFICATION DUTY onto a party holding no facts. This lens is detection and scope PROVENANCE. Reference the W33 entry explicitly.
